```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#### Set up filepath, notation and packages
rm(list=ls())

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
options(scipen = 100, digits = 4)

##Load packages
pacman::p_load( "tidyverse","readxl","ggplot2","ggalluvial","ggrepel","gridExtra","cowplot","survey","dplyr","scales","RColorBrewer",
                "networkD3", "grid","fastDummies","tidyr",
                "foreign","haven","corrplot","forcats","vtable","srvyr","readr","vtable","data.table","kableExtra",
                "rpart", "rpart.plot", "caret", "randomForest", "colorspace", "openxlsx")

##Set filepath
setwd("/Users/darcyrao/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-Bill&MelindaGatesFoundation/Pathways - GE Data & Insights/Modeling/Kenya 2022 DHS/")

## Read in final segmentation solutions
final_model_urban <- "urban_round6_u5" # list the folder name for the final model run
final_model_rural <- "rural_round6_u5" # list the folder name for the final model run

kclass_urban <- "cluster_k4" # use the 4-class solution
kclass_rural <- "cluster_k4" # use the 4-class solution

urban <- readRDS(file.path("Solutions/KE 2022 (women with kids - Final solution)/LCA", final_model_urban,"dhs.seg_reform.rds"))
urban[, class := as.factor(get(kclass_urban))]
urban$class <- paste0("U",urban$class)

rural <- readRDS(file.path("Solutions/KE 2022 (women with kids - Final solution)/LCA", final_model_rural, "dhs.seg_reform.rds"))
rural[, class := as.factor(get(kclass_rural))]
rural$class <- paste0("R",rural$class)

## Load in original DHS data to pull in other variables and merge with the objects above containing class variables
vulnerability <- readRDS("Data/Constructed data/4_Kenya_DHS_vulnerability.rds")
outcomes <- readRDS("Data/Constructed data/1_Kenya_DHS_outcomes.rds")
dhs.full <- merge(vulnerability, outcomes, by="caseid", all.x=T)

dhs.seg.urban <- urban %>%
  dplyr::select(caseid, class) %>%
  left_join(dhs.full, by = "caseid")
dhs.seg.urban <- as.data.table(dhs.seg.urban)

dhs.seg.rural <- rural %>%
  dplyr::select(caseid, class) %>%
  left_join(dhs.full, by = "caseid")
dhs.seg.rural <- as.data.table(dhs.seg.rural)

ken <- rbind.data.frame(dhs.seg.urban, dhs.seg.rural)

## Pull out the k-class solution and rename the segments based on approximate vulnerability level (eyeballed from plots)

# R1 => R1-K
# R3 => R2-K
# R2 => R3-K
# R4 => R4-K

# U3 => U1-K
# U4 => U2-K
# U1 => U3-K
# U2 => U4-K

ken <- ken %>% 
  mutate(class = case_when(
    class == "U3" ~ "U1-K",
    class == "U4" ~ "U2-K",
    class == "U1" ~ "U3-K",
    class == "U2" ~ "U4-K",
    class == "R1" ~ "R1-K",
    class == "R3" ~ "R2-K",
    class == "R2" ~ "R3-K",
    class == "R4" ~ "R4-K"))

# Save dataset with segments
saveRDS(ken, file="Data/Constructed data/ken.seg.rds")

##Read in variable mapping excel
const <- data.table(read.xlsx("Analysis plans and methods documentation/9_Kenya_DHS_construct_mapping_PCA_to_LCA.xlsx",sheet = 'Sheet 1'))
# Read in variable label from data dictionary
dict <- data.table(read.xlsx("Analysis plans and methods documentation/0_Kenya_DHS_Data_Dictionary.xlsx",sheet = 'Vulnerabilities_full_list_SS', startRow = 7))
# Merge with variable mapping
const <- dict %>% select(variable.label, variable.name) %>%
  rename(var.name = variable.name) %>%
  right_join(const, by = "var.name") %>%
  mutate(variable.label = if_else(var.name == "hh.fin.assist.yn", "Life in the community and support", variable.label)) # hard code label for hh.fin.assist.yn to be life in the community and support

 
# Keep only final LCA vars
  const <- const[str_detect(tolower(const$urban_currentLCA), "^keep") | str_detect(tolower(const$rural_currentLCA), "^keep")]  
  const <- const[!duplicated(const$f.var.name),]

  lca.var <- const$f.var.name

subset_var <- const[const$f.var.name %in% lca.var, c("f.var.name", "var.type")]
bin.var <- subset_var$f.var.name[subset_var$var.type=='binary']
cat.var <- subset_var$f.var.name[str_detect(subset_var$var.type, 'categorical')]

## Recode some variables to be coded correctly
tabulated_columns <- lapply(lca.var, function(col) {
    table(ken[[col]])
})
names(tabulated_columns) <- lca.var # Naming the list with the column names for clarity
tabulated_columns # Print the tabulated results

# yes/no vars to 1/0
for(var.i in bin.var){
  
  if("yes" %in% unique(ken[,get(var.i)])){
    ken[, (var.i) := as.character(get(var.i))]
    ken[get(var.i) == "yes", (var.i) := "1"]
    ken[get(var.i) == "no", (var.i) := "0"]
  }
  ken[, (var.i) := as.numeric(get(var.i))]  
  
}

# change some numeric variables to apply labels
ken <- ken %>% mutate(freq.tv = factor(freq.tv, levels = c(0, 1, 2), labels = c("Not at all", "Less than once a week", "At least once a week")))

# Create a former province variable
#load data mapping county to former province
county_to_province <- read_excel("Data/kenya_county_to_province.xlsx")
county_to_province$county <- tolower(county_to_province$county)
county_to_province$county[county_to_province$county=="taita-taveta"] <- "taita taveta"
ken$county <- ken$v024
ken <- ken %>%
  left_join(county_to_province, by ="county")

# Create an age cat variable
ken <- ken %>% mutate(age_cat = cut(age.yrs, breaks = c(0, 19, 24, 34, 49), labels = c("15-19", "20-24", "25-34", "35-49")))

## Apply survey weights and define urban/rural strata
ken_urban <- ken %>% filter(hh.urban == 1)
ken_rural <- ken %>% filter(hh.urban == 0)

urban.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data = subset(ken, hh.urban == 1))
rural.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data = subset(ken, hh.urban == 0))
ken.des <-svydesign(id=~v021, strata=~v023, weights=~wt, data=ken)

## Load list of outcomes
outcomes.df <- data.table(read.xlsx("Analysis plans and methods documentation/0_Kenya_DHS_Data_Dictionary.xlsx",sheet = "Outcomes (updated)"))
outcomes.df <- outcomes.df[keep == "Keep"]
outcomes.df <- outcomes.df %>% filter(!(variable.name %in% c("birthwgt.last.cat3")))
# filter to list of outcomes that are binary
ken.outcomes <- ken %>% select(outcomes.df$variable.name)
outcomes <- outcomes.df$variable.name
outcomes <- outcomes[apply(ken.outcomes,2,function(x) { all(na.omit(x) %in% 0:1) })]

```

## 1. Distribution Overview

### 1.1. Distribution of rural segments
```{r}
rural.seg.tab <- svytable(~class, design = rural.des)
rural.seg.pie <- as.data.frame(rural.seg.tab)

rural.seg.pie <- rural.seg.pie %>%
  mutate(percent = round((Freq / sum(Freq)) * 100, digits = 0))%>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(class)) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_freq = cumsum(Freq),
         midpoint = cumulative_freq - (Freq/2))

# Define the color palette
nseg_rural <- length(unique(ken_rural$class))
rural_palette <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(n=nseg_rural, "BuGn")

ggplot(rural.seg.pie, aes(x = factor(1), fill = class)) + 
  geom_bar(aes(weight = Freq), width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") + 
  geom_text(aes(y = midpoint, label = paste0(round(percent, 1), "%")), color = "black", size = 3.5) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = rural_palette) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Segment") +
  theme_void() +
  ggtitle("Distribution of Rural Segments [Weight Adjusted]")

rural.seg.pie
```

### 1.4. Geographic distribution
Note that 60% of women in the smallest segment (U4) reside in the former North Eastern Province, which they make up 31% of. The next smallest segment is R4, of whom 47% reside in Rift Valley, making up 11% of women with kids under 5 in that former province, while 20% reside in North Eastern, making up 50% of women in that former province.
```{r}

seg.region <- as.data.frame(seg.region)

  mutate(perc = round((Freq / sum(Freq)) * 100, digits = 0)) %>%
```

## 2. Means of outcomes by segment
### 2.1. Overall profiles
```{r, echo=FALSE}
## Means by segment
# Initialize an empty list to store results
results_list <- list()

# Loop through each variable in outcomes.list and calculate weighted means
for (var in outcomes) {
  # Use svyby to calculate the mean of each outcome by 'class'
  result <- svyby(formula = as.formula(paste0("~", var)),
                  by = ~class, 
                  design = ken.des, 
                  FUN = svymean, 
                  na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Store the result in the list and name it after the variable
  results_list[[var]] <- result
}

# Combine the results from the list into a single data frame
cluster_means_outcomes <- as.data.frame(do.call(cbind, lapply(results_list, function(x) x[, 2])))  # Extract means
cluster_means_outcomes$class <- results_list[[1]]$class

# Pivot to longer
cluster_means_outcomes <- cluster_means_outcomes %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(outcomes), names_to = "outcome", values_to = "cluster_mean")

## overall means
# Initialize an empty list to store results
means_outcomes_overall <- cbind.data.frame(outcome = outcomes, overall_mean = NA)

# Loop through each variable in outcomes.list and calculate weighted means
for (var in outcomes) {
  # Use mean to calculate the mean of each outcome by 'class'
  result <- svymean(x = as.formula(paste0("~", var)),
                  design = ken.des, 
                  na.rm = TRUE)
  result <- as.vector(result[1])
  
  # Store the result in the list and name it after the variable
  means_outcomes_overall$overall_mean[means_outcomes_overall$outcome == var] <- result
}

# Merge the two datasets
outcomes_means <- left_join(cluster_means_outcomes, means_outcomes_overall, by = "outcome")

# Calculate the differences between cluster and ovearll means and percent differences
outcomes_means <- outcomes_means %>%
  mutate(difference = cluster_mean - overall_mean,
    percent_difference = (difference / overall_mean))

# Merge in category from the outcomes sheet
outcomes_means_cat <- outcomes.df %>% dplyr::select(Category, variable.name) %>%
    group_by(variable.name) %>%
    rename(outcome = variable.name) %>%
    right_join(outcomes_means, by = "outcome") %>%
    ungroup() 

# define class as a factor
outcomes_means_cat$class <- factor(outcomes_means_cat$class)

```

### 2.2. Outcomes by segment
#### 2.2.1 Reproductive and sexual health
```{r}

rsh.outcomes <- outcomes.df %>% 
  dplyr::select(Category, variable.name, label) %>%
  filter(Category =="Reproductive and sexual health") %>%
  select(variable.name, label) %>%
  rename(outcome = variable.name)

results <- list()

for (outcome in rsh.outcomes$outcome) {
  outcome_table <- svytable(~class + get(outcome), design = ken.des)
  outcome_df <- as.data.frame(outcome_table)
  
  outcome_df <- outcome_df %>%
    group_by(class) %>%
    mutate(perc = round((Freq / sum(Freq)) * 100, digits = 0)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  outcome_df$outcome <- outcome
  results[[outcome]] <- outcome_df
}

# Combine all results into a single data frame
prop.rsh.outcomes <- bind_rows(results)

# Merge in label
prop.rsh.outcomes <- prop.rsh.outcomes %>%
  left_join(rsh.outcomes, by = "outcome")

# Change 0/1 to yes/no
prop.rsh.outcomes <- prop.rsh.outcomes %>%
  rename(value = get.outcome.) %>%
  mutate(value = case_when(
    value == 0 ~ "No",
    value == 1 ~ "Yes"
  )) 

rsh.outcomes.plotlist <- list()
for(out in rsh.outcomes$label){
rsh.outcomes.plotlist[[out]] <- prop.rsh.outcomes %>%
    filter(label == out) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = class, y = perc, fill = value)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(perc, 0), "%")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.5) +
    labs(x = "Segment", y = "Percentage", title = out) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#b4adaa","#03859b")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 9), 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
}
  rsh.outcomes.plotlist
  
  
```

#### 2.2.3 Child care behavior
```{r}

child.care.outcomes <- outcomes.df %>% 
  dplyr::select(Category, variable.name, label) %>%
  filter(Category =="Child care behavior") %>%
  select(variable.name, label) %>%
  rename(outcome = variable.name)

results <- list()

for (outcome in child.care.outcomes$outcome) {
  outcome_table <- svytable(~class + get(outcome), design = ken.des)
  outcome_df <- as.data.frame(outcome_table)
  
  outcome_df <- outcome_df %>%
    group_by(class) %>%
    mutate(perc = round((Freq / sum(Freq)) * 100, digits = 0)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  outcome_df$outcome <- outcome
  results[[outcome]] <- outcome_df
}

# Combine all results into a single data frame
prop.child.care.outcomes <- bind_rows(results)

# Merge in label
prop.child.care.outcomes <- prop.child.care.outcomes %>%
  left_join(child.care.outcomes, by = "outcome")

# Change 0/1 to yes/no
prop.child.care.outcomes <- prop.child.care.outcomes %>%
  rename(value = get.outcome.) %>%
  mutate(value = case_when(
    value == 0 ~ "No",
    value == 1 ~ "Yes"
  )) 

child.care.outcomes.plotlist <- list()
for(out in child.care.outcomes$label){
child.care.outcomes.plotlist[[out]] <- prop.child.care.outcomes %>%
    filter(label == out) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = class, y = perc, fill = value)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack", width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(perc, 0), "%")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.5) +
    labs(x = "Segment", y = "Percentage", title = out) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#b4adaa","#03859b")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 9), 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
}
  child.care.outcomes.plotlist
  
  
```

## 3. Vulnerability factors

### 3.1. Binary heatmap
Note that variables are not all "oriented" the same way, so a higher proportion for some is protective, while for others signals increased vulnerability.
```{r, echo = F, fig.height=10}

results <- list()

for (var in bin.var) {
  vuln_table <- svyby(~get(var), ~class, design = ken.des, svymean, na.rm = T)
  vuln_df <- as.data.frame(vuln_table)
  
  vuln_df$variable <- var
  results[[var]] <- vuln_df
}

# Combine all results into a single data frame
prop.binvar <- bind_rows(results)

# Merge in domain
const.merge <- const %>% select(category, var.name) %>%
  rename(variable = var.name)
prop.binvar <- prop.binvar %>%
  rename(mean = "get(var)") %>%
  left_join(const.merge, by = "variable") %>%
  select(class, mean, variable, category)
  
# Plot
  heatmap <- ggplot(prop.binvar, aes(x = factor(class), y = variable, fill = mean)) +
    geom_tile() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(category), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    # facet_wrap(~category, scales = "free_y", ncol =) + 
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#313695", mid = "#FFFFBF", high = "#A50026", midpoint = 0.5, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1)) +
  labs(title = '', x = '', y = '', fill = 'Proportion within\ncluster') +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 5),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 5),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, size = 5),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.8, "lines")) 
    
heatmap
```
